prompt: Which technology should control a planner card’s visual spacing?
explanation: CSS controls presentation while HTML supplies meaningful structure.

prompt: Which HTML element connects styles.css as a stylesheet?
explanation: A stylesheet link belongs in the document head and uses rel and href.

prompt: Which selector targets elements with class="card"?
explanation: A dot introduces a class selector; an ID selector begins with #.

prompt: How should the class name appear in HTML for the selector .card?
explanation: The dot is CSS selector syntax and is not part of the HTML class name.

prompt: Which is a valid CSS declaration?
explanation: A declaration separates the property and value with a colon.

prompt: What encloses a CSS rule’s declarations?
explanation: Declarations sit inside braces after the selector.

prompt: Which property changes text foreground color?
explanation: The color property sets the foreground used by text.

prompt: A stylesheet request returns 404. What should you inspect first?

choices.text: The link’s file path and saved filename

explanation: A missing resource is commonly caused by an incorrect path or filename.

prompt: Where can you inspect a crossed-out CSS declaration?
explanation: Developer tools show matched rules and indicate overridden or invalid declarations.

prompt: Does styling a div to look like a heading make it a semantic heading?

choices.text: No, use an appropriate heading element
Only when the font is bold
Yes, any large text becomes h1

explanation: CSS appearance does not replace meaningful HTML structure.

prompt: In equal origin, importance, and layer, which selector is most specific?
explanation: An ID selector has greater specificity than a class or element selector under these equal conditions.

prompt: Two normal rules in the same layer use the same selector. Which color wins?

choices.text: The color in the later rule

explanation: When preceding cascade criteria and specificity tie, later source order wins.

prompt: Does the order of class names in class="large pink" determine which conflicting CSS rule wins?
explanation: HTML class-attribute order is not stylesheet source order.

prompt: Which property normally inherits from a parent?
explanation: Text color normally inherits; spacing and border widths do not normally do so.

prompt: Which selector targets only direct paragraph children of .card?
explanation: The child combinator > restricts matching to direct children.

prompt: Which selector can match a paragraph nested several levels inside .card?
explanation: The descendant combinator matches descendants regardless of nesting depth.

prompt: A child has its own color declaration. What happens to its parent’s inherited color?

choices.text: The child’s declaration can replace the inherited value

explanation: Inheritance supplies a value when the child does not receive its own applicable value.

prompt: Why is “the last rule always wins” incomplete?

choices.text: Earlier cascade steps can decide the winner

explanation: Origin, importance, layers, and specificity can decide before source order.

prompt: What is a good first step when a style unexpectedly loses?

choices.text: Inspect the competing rules and cascade

explanation: Inspecting the actual matched rules identifies the cause instead of hiding it.

prompt: Which selector expresses the hover state of a card?
explanation: A pseudo-class can match an element in a particular state.

prompt: Which space is inside an element’s border?
explanation: Padding separates content from the inside of the border.

prompt: Which space lies outside the border?
explanation: Margin separates the outside of a box from surrounding boxes.

prompt: With content-box, width: 200px, 10px padding per side and 2px borders per side, what is the border-box width?
explanation: Add both paddings and both borders to the 200px content width.

prompt: With border-box and width: 200px, does padding increase the declared border-box width?

choices.text: No, padding is included in the 200px

explanation: Border-box includes padding and borders in the declared width.

prompt: Which rule sets border-box for elements and their pseudo-elements?
explanation: The universal selectors include pseudo-elements explicitly and set the sizing model.

prompt: Which property puts an upper limit on an element’s width?
explanation: max-width constrains the width without requiring that width at every viewport size.

prompt: A flex item refuses to shrink around a long title. Which sizing rule may help?
explanation: An automatic minimum can prevent shrinking; min-width: 0 removes that constraint.

prompt: Which rule helps an unbroken long task title wrap?
explanation: Overflow wrapping permits breaks that can avoid horizontal overflow.

prompt: Can adjacent vertical block margins collapse in normal flow?

choices.text: Yes, under the applicable margin-collapsing rules

explanation: Normal block flow can collapse adjoining vertical margins; flex/grid item margins do not collapse with each other.

prompt: Why test a fixed-width card on a narrow viewport?

choices.text: Its width may exceed the available space

explanation: A fixed width can force page overflow when the viewport is smaller.

prompt: Which declaration gives text a system font with a generic fallback?
explanation: A font-family list provides a preferred family and fallback.

prompt: What does rem refer to?
explanation: rem units are relative to the root font size.

prompt: What is an advantage of a unitless line-height?

choices.text: It scales with each element’s font size

explanation: A unitless multiplier computes line height from the element’s own font size.

prompt: What does font-weight primarily change?
explanation: Font weight changes how light or heavy the type appears.

prompt: In clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.5rem), which value is the maximum?
explanation: clamp takes a minimum, a preferred value, and a maximum.

prompt: Is max-width: 65ch an exact limit of 65 characters per line?

choices.text: No, ch is based on a font glyph metric
Yes, every font has identical character widths

explanation: The ch unit uses the zero glyph’s advance measure, not a character counter.

prompt: What should accompany a red overdue-task color?

choices.text: A readable status word or other non-color cue

explanation: Meaning should remain understandable without relying only on color.

prompt: Why can fixed-height text cards fail at 200% zoom?

choices.text: Enlarged text can be clipped or overflow

explanation: Text needs room to grow and wrap when users enlarge it.

prompt: What should you evaluate when choosing a muted text color?

choices.text: Its contrast against the actual background

explanation: Contrast is a relationship between foreground and background colors.

prompt: Which property changes line spacing rather than text color?
explanation: Line height controls the line box height and affects vertical readability.

prompt: Where should display: flex be placed to arrange a toolbar’s children?

choices.text: Only on the browser body in every case

explanation: The container establishes the flex formatting context for direct children.

prompt: Which children become flex items?
explanation: Flexbox lays out direct children of the flex container.

prompt: What determines the main-axis direction?
explanation: The flex direction establishes whether the main axis follows a row or a column.

prompt: Which property distributes space on the flex main axis?
explanation: justify-content handles distribution along the main axis.

prompt: Which property aligns flex items on the cross axis?
explanation: align-items controls cross-axis alignment for the items.

prompt: Which rule permits flex items to move onto additional lines?
explanation: Wrapping allows items to form multiple flex lines.

prompt: What does gap control in a flex container?
explanation: Gap supplies gutters without needing a margin on every child.

prompt: Does visual reordering with Flexbox reliably change keyboard focus order?
explanation: Visual order and source-based navigation can differ.

prompt: What does flex-grow describe?

choices.text: How many HTML children it creates
How an item shares positive free space

explanation: The grow factor participates in distributing available free space.

prompt: With flex-direction: column, is justify-content necessarily horizontal?

choices.text: No, it follows the vertical main axis in the usual writing mode

explanation: The main axis follows flex-direction, so column changes the direction of distribution.

prompt: Which declaration establishes a grid container?
explanation: The display property creates the grid formatting context.

prompt: Which property defines explicit column tracks?
explanation: Grid template columns defines the sizes and structure of explicit columns.

prompt: What does fr represent in grid track sizing?

choices.text: A share of available remaining space

explanation: Fractional units divide remaining space among flexible tracks.

prompt: What does repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)) create?

choices.text: Two equally flexible columns with a zero minimum

explanation: The repeat count is two and each track uses the same flexible sizing function.

prompt: Why can minmax(0, 1fr) help avoid content-driven track expansion?

choices.text: It removes the automatic minimum for that track

explanation: A zero minimum allows the track to shrink instead of imposing an automatic content minimum.

prompt: Which property adds gutters between grid tracks?
explanation: Gap sets spacing between grid tracks.

prompt: Does moving a grid item visually guarantee the same reading order?

choices.text: Only if a border is present

explanation: Visual placement can diverge from source order, so structure should remain logical.

prompt: Which tool can create an adaptive number of card columns?
explanation: auto-fit with a minimum track size can adapt the number of tracks.

prompt: What does grid-column control on an item?
explanation: The item’s grid-column property places it across grid column lines.

prompt: Why is a two-column grid not automatically phone-friendly?

choices.text: CSS disables wrapping in every grid
The available columns may be too narrow for the content

explanation: Responsive choices must follow the needs of actual content.

prompt: Which HTML metadata helps mobile browsers use the device width?
explanation: The viewport declaration enables the intended mobile layout viewport behavior.

prompt: In a mobile-first stylesheet, where do you usually put the simplest narrow layout?
explanation: Base rules establish a useful layout before wider-screen enhancements.

prompt: When does @media (min-width: 48rem) apply?

choices.text: Only on a named tablet model

explanation: A min-width condition includes the threshold and wider viewports.

prompt: What should guide a layout breakpoint?

choices.text: Where the content needs a different arrangement

explanation: Content-based breakpoints respond to actual layout needs.

prompt: Which common image rules prevent an image exceeding its container while preserving proportions?
explanation: A width limit constrains the image and automatic height preserves its intrinsic aspect ratio.

prompt: A schedule table is wider than a phone. What is a useful approach?

choices.text: Give the table a local horizontal scroll container

explanation: Local scrolling can preserve the table while keeping the main page within the viewport.

prompt: Which content is especially useful for responsive testing?
explanation: Long content reveals shrinking, wrapping, and overflow problems.

prompt: Why also test zoom when checking responsive design?

choices.text: Users may need enlarged content and controls

explanation: Responsive testing should include the way users enlarge and read content.

prompt: Does overflow: hidden fix every layout overflow accessibly?

choices.text: No, it may conceal content and controls
Yes, it always solves the cause

explanation: Clipping can hide the symptom while making information unavailable.

prompt: How many columns does the notebook example use below its 48rem breakpoint?
explanation: The base grid has one implicit column; the media query adds the two-column template.

prompt: Which selector is designed for focus that should be visibly indicated?
explanation: The focus-visible pseudo-class supports a clear focus indicator when the browser determines it is needed.

prompt: Why is a hover-only indicator insufficient?

choices.text: Keyboard and touch users may not trigger hover

explanation: Useful interaction feedback must cover input methods beyond a pointer.

prompt: What does outline-offset change?

choices.text: The distance between an outline and the element

explanation: Outline offset separates the indicator from the element’s border edge.

prompt: Does a gray disabled-looking style prevent a button action?

choices.text: Yes, if gray is dark enough
No, visual styling alone does not disable behavior

explanation: Use native disabled semantics or appropriate behavior as well as appearance.

prompt: Which media query responds to a request for less motion?
explanation: The reduced-motion preference can be used to simplify nonessential movement.

prompt: Why transition only the properties that need it?

choices.text: To keep feedback intentional and avoid unintended animations

explanation: Targeted transitions are easier to predict and maintain.

prompt: Is removing all focus outlines without replacement a good default?

choices.text: No, it can hide keyboard position
Only if the page is colorful
Yes, buttons do not need focus

explanation: Keyboard users need a visible way to know which control is focused.

prompt: Which native selector can style a disabled form control?
explanation: The disabled pseudo-class matches controls in the native disabled state.

prompt: Does reduced-motion support eliminate the need to review default animation?

choices.text: Yes, all animation is automatically safe
No, defaults should also be thoughtful

explanation: Preference handling supplements good defaults rather than replacing them.

prompt: Which practical check directly tests focus visibility?

choices.text: Navigate controls with Tab and Shift+Tab

explanation: Keyboard navigation reveals whether focus is visible and follows a sensible order.

prompt: How do CSS custom property names begin?
explanation: Custom property names use the -- prefix.

prompt: Which expression reads the custom property --accent?
explanation: The var function substitutes a custom property value.

prompt: Where can a shared theme token be declared for broad use?
explanation: Root-level custom properties can inherit throughout the document.

prompt: Do ordinary custom properties normally inherit?

choices.text: Only when their names are uppercase

explanation: Custom properties normally inherit and participate in the cascade.

prompt: What happens when .card--calm declares a local --accent value?

choices.text: Descendants can use that overridden token value
All cards must use it globally

explanation: A local custom property changes the value in that element’s scope and inherited subtree.

prompt: Which is a semantic token name?
explanation: A semantic token communicates the design role of its value.

prompt: What is the fallback in var(--accent, navy)?
explanation: The second argument is used when the variable cannot supply a usable substitution under the variable rules.

prompt: Will a var() fallback repair every value that is unsuitable for the final property?

choices.text: Yes, it is a complete type checker
It converts every value to pixels

explanation: A substituted value can still make the final declaration invalid.

prompt: Why extract repeated spacing into a token?
explanation: A shared decision can be changed in one place and reviewed across components.

prompt: What should you inspect after changing a shared accent token?

choices.text: All affected text, borders, focus states, and surfaces

explanation: A token can affect many uses, including color relationships and interaction indicators.

prompt: What should happen to the HTML planner’s semantic structure during styling?

choices.text: Replace every element with a div

explanation: Presentation changes should retain meaningful structure and controls.

prompt: Which layout model is a good fit for a wrapping toolbar?
explanation: Flexbox handles a one-dimensional group that may wrap.

prompt: Which layout model suits a two-dimensional card arrangement?
explanation: Grid provides rows and columns for arranging cards.

prompt: What should the project README disclose about task saving?

choices.text: It works because a button is pink
It is not implemented in this static phase

explanation: Static styling does not implement storage or submission behavior.

prompt: Which set of checks best reviews the responsive project?

choices.text: Narrow and wide widths, zoom, long content, and keyboard use

explanation: These checks exercise the real layout and interaction constraints.

prompt: What should you do if a wide table makes the whole page scroll sideways?

choices.text: Keep table overflow local and inspect the layout

explanation: A local overflow container can preserve table access without forcing page-wide overflow.

prompt: What is a useful Git milestone for this project?

choices.text: Save all work under an unrelated filename

explanation: A focused commit records a meaningful, reviewable step.

prompt: Does a passing MCQ score prove the planner works on mobile?

choices.text: Only if the score is above 50%

explanation: Recall and practical implementation are different forms of evidence.

prompt: What should a before/after comparison explain?

choices.text: Why the layout and readability improved
Only the number of CSS lines

explanation: Explaining decisions shows understanding beyond copying styles.

prompt: What is the best response to a keyboard focus issue found in review?

choices.text: Fix it and document the change

explanation: The project review should lead to concrete improvements and a record of what was learned.
